chunks: Muhammad ibn Hammam (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik narrated to us, saying: 'Abbad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Ya'la, from Zurara, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah saying:

Indeed, the Qa'im has a period of occultation before his rising. I asked: 'Why?' He said: 'He fears.' -And he gestured with his hand to his stomach.- Then he said: 'O Zurara, he is the Expected One, and there is doubt about his birth. Some say his father died without leaving offspring, some say he was carried (in the womb), some say he is hidden, and some say he was born some years before his father's death. He is the Expected One, but Allah loves to test the hearts of the Shia, so at that time the false-claimants will doubt, O Zurara.'

Zurara said: I said: 'May I be your ransom, if I live to see that time, what should I do?' He said: 'O Zurara, when you live to see that time, pray with this supplication: O Allah, make me know You, for if You do not make me know You, I will not know Your Prophet. O Allah, make me know Your Messenger, for if You do not make me know Your Messenger, I will not know Your Authority. O Allah, make me know Your Authority, for if You do not make me know Your Authority, I will deviate from my religion.'

Then he said: 'O Zurara, it is necessary that a young boy be killed in Medina.' I said: 'May I be your ransom, is he not the one who will be killed by the army of al-Sufyani?' He said: 'No, but he will be killed by the army of So-and-so. This army will come out until it enters Medina, and people will not know why it entered. Then they will take the boy and kill him. When they kill him unjustly, offensively, and wrongfully, Allah will not delay punishing them, and at that time the deliverance will be expected.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the occultation and the predicted events in Medina according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* establishes the theological basis for the Major Occultation, framing the doubt regarding Imam al-Mahdi’s birth as a divine trial to distinguish true believers from the 'false ones.' It links spiritual preparedness—emphasized through the specific supplication for recognizing the Imam—to the eschatological sign of a young boy’s martyrdom in Medina, which triggers the final wait for deliverance.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (6) Muhammad bin Hammam narrated from Ja’far bin Muhammad bin Malik from Abbad bin Ya’qoob from Yahya bin Ya’la that Zurara had said: I heard Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) saying:

“Al-Qa’im (as) will disappear before his rising.” I asked: “Why?” He said: “He fears (people) although he is the expected one. O Zurara, his birth is suspected. Some say that his father has died without leaving offspring, some say that he has disappeared and others say that he has born some years before his father’s death. He is the expected imam but Allah will try the hearts of the Shia and then might those have doubted, who follow falsehood.”

I said: “May I die for you! If I live until that time, what shall I do then?” He said: “O Zurarra, when you live until then, pray with this prayer: (O Allah, let me know You because if You do not let me know You, I can never know Your prophet. O Allah, let me know Your prophet because if You do not let me know Your prophet, I can never know Your authority. O Allah, let me know Your authority because if You do not let me know Your authority, I shall deviate from my religion.”

Then he said: “O Zurara, a young boy will be killed in Medina then.” I said: “Is he not the one, who will be killed by the army of as-Sufyani?” He said: “No, but he will be killed by the army of bani so and so. This army will enter into Medina and people will not know why the army has come. Then the young boy will be taken and killed unjustly and offensively. When the boy is killed, Allah will not respite them and then the deliverance will be expected soon.” The same was narrated by Muhammad bin Ya’qoob al-Kulayni from Ali bin Ibraheem bin Hashim from al-Hasan bin Musa al-Khashshab from Abdullah bin Musa from Abdullah bin Bukayr from Zurara from Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as). Also it was narrated by Muhammad bin Ya’qoob from al-Husayn bin Ahmad from Ahmad bin Hilal from Uthman bin Eessa from Khalid bin Nujayh from Zurara from Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as).
